sourceNote: The mesh assets/models/mouse/mouse.glb (assets/models/mouse/README.md), with new quad faces on each arm from the shoulder line to the wrist. tools/blender/wind_arms.py makes these faces. The other faces and mouse.glb stay unchanged.
paintedNote: The weights of the clavicles and the arms are the automatic weights of Blender with the Weight Paint fixes of tools/blender/wind_arms.py. The vertices on the bones of paintedLower keep the rule weights, as on the rabbit and the polar bear, because the seated bind of the app depends on them.

armSegments.note: Each upper arm and each forearm has 4 deform segments, and each elbow and wrist a helper bone of this length in units, which spans the three rings of its joint in the bind. The app turns them from the joints of the pose (poseArm() of src/models/studio-rig.ts).

name: Mouse

app.note: The scale puts the standing skull top (0.9485 u) at 0.812 m, 0.856045 m for each unit, with the standing shoulder joints at 0.507635 m (the entry of the mouse in ANIMALS). The reach is the reach of the arm factor, from the shoulder joint to the middle of the palm.

armFactorNote: The factor 1 keeps the arm length, because the rig with arm segments does not stretch the arms. The arms of mouse-arms.glb are 1.25 times longer than the source arms (step_shape() of tools/blender/violin_arms.py), so the reach is 0.293 m. The mouse plays a smaller oboe (SpeciesParams.oboeScale, SPECIES_WIND_HOLDS.mouse of src/pose/winds.ts).
legFactorNote: The legs keep the length of the mesh. Do not stretch the legs: change the chair. The seat of the legs of the seated bind is 0.076 m.
jointsNote: The places are in the studio units and axes of the source pose: 1 unit from the soles to the top of the ears, the soles at y = 0, +z forward, +x the left side. The right side mirrors the left side. The joints of the elbow, the wrist, and the paw are the joints of the longer arms of wind_arms.py.

studio.note: The seated posture of design 5.2: the thigh slopes 25 degrees down and 15 degrees out, so that the oboe has room between the knees, and the shin is vertical (tools/rig/leg_turns.py <config> 25 15 0). tailBind turns the tail root 24 degrees below the level, so that the loop of the tail lies flat on the floor behind the chair.

tail.note: The vertices within radius of the line of the tail bones, and behind the plane z = behind, follow the tail bones. The loop of the tail lies up to 0.077 u from the line, so the radius is 0.09 u.

haunch.note: The part of the thigh weight that goes to the hips grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height, so that the round haunch stays on the hips.

weights.rigidNote: The corners of the thin face from the neck to the top of the left shoulder take the mean of their weights (rigid_faces() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), so that the face does not turn over. The point is the middle of the face in the units of the source.
weights.note: Beyond the plane |x| = armSplit, only the free arm follows the arm bones. Above headFrom (the chin), each vertex follows the head only. The ears join the head below the skull top, so earBase lies above the head and the ears follow the head.

refine.ringsNote: The config has no rings. pnpm rig-mesh mouse --check lists the thin faces near the joints as candidates for a ring (check.thin).

colors.note: A dark face in the eye box is an eye. A pink face in the nose box is the nose and takes the gloss. The nose box also sets the tip of the nose, because the front-most vertex of the head is the tip of a whisker.

tone.note: Each plain face takes the hue and the chroma of the species color of its band (SPECIES_COLORS.mouse) and keeps its lightness, as for the panda. A row is [L, dL, da, db] in Oklab. The pink parts have a chroma above 0.05, so they keep their colors.

chair.note: The seat is level, and its top is the lowest point of the seated body over the seat, with no shin, foot, or tail. The half width holds the haunch. The front edge lies behind the shins, and the back edge holds the back of the haunch.

sit.note: The values of the panda and the hippo.
